actions.prompt: Fen Maro recognizes you from their journal. They offer you a letter to deliver to Warden Holt at Outpost Balor.

options.label: Accept
options.description: Take Fen's letter to Warden Holt. Fen will also mark a supply cache location.

options.label: Decline
options.description: You're not heading back to Balor anytime soon.

lines: Fen presses the worn envelope into your hands. Their fingers tremble slightly.
'Thank you. And the cache — it's near the old watchtower, hidden in a collapsed section of wall. My squad's gear. Better than anything in the shops.'
'Tell Holt I'm sorry. That's all I ask.'

actions.text: Fen nods slowly. 'I understand. Maybe another time.' They turn back to the window.

lines: Sable places a dark, softly pulsing seed in your palm. It's warm to the touch.
'An Umbral Seed. From the deepest Nightside. Where the planet's heartbeat is strongest.'
'I don't know what it'll become in the light. But you should have it. A gift between worlds.'
Fen listens in silence as you describe the cache. The bedrolls in formation. The cold field stove. The team photo.
They close their eyes for a long moment. When they open them again, something has shifted.
'You brought their memory back. That's... that's enough. Thank you.'
'I know these perimeters better than anyone alive. If you need a guide, or someone to watch your back out there — I'm ready.'
The Residential Quarter is darker than before. The Array's automated street lighting is down to essential power only — warm pools of lamplight instead of the even grid-glow.
Groups of people cluster on the stoops, talking. You catch fragments: contingency plans, food sharing arrangements, who has what skills for what the Ring now has to do for itself.
Unbounded traders have set up a small exchange near the corner. They look less out of place now than they used to.
The Residential Quarter has changed in small ways. Bioluminescent plant cuttings — new cultivars, grown from Underlumen-adjacent root stock — sit in window boxes, glowing faintly blue-green.
A shared notice board has been set up at the corner: Ring community postings sit alongside Unbounded trade announcements and, in one corner, a small Array advisory in clean typeset.
Nobody who lives here looks entirely comfortable with the new arrangement. Nobody looks unhappy enough to leave.
The Residential Quarter has a new feature: a Ring Authority monitoring post at the main corner, staffed by two officers who check transit credentials with polite efficiency.
The streets are cleaner. There are fewer people out — or perhaps the same number, moving faster, with less time to linger.
The bioluminescent signals that Sable's people used to mark safe passages in the dark are gone. Painted over, or simply left to fade.

actions.prompt: Sable studies you as you approach. She can tell you've found something.

options.label: Share the network topology
options.description: Give Sable the Array's complete infrastructure map. The Unbounded will know exactly where to cut.

lines: Sable takes the data tablet. Her eyes move across the schematic — relay stations, power conduits, redundancy pathways — and something shifts in her expression. Not surprise. Recognition.
'My grandmother drew maps like this. One Lighthouse at a time. But the same idea: find where the power flows, and find where it can be stopped.'
'This is everything. Every connection point, every dependency chain. We can plan a shutdown that doesn't kill the people who depend on the Array's climate systems. Controlled. Precise. Surgical.'
'The Unbounded have been waiting three generations for this. You just gave us the blueprint.'
She presses a sol component into your hands — etched with Unbounded circuit patterns.
'My people made this from the same principles: know the system, exploit the weakness. It will serve you well against the Array's guardians.'

actions.text: Sable nods. 'When you're ready. The Array isn't going anywhere — that's rather the problem.'

lines: Sable's eyes track the authentication sequences running across the data surface. She doesn't touch it.
'Central Node Override Protocols. MERIDIAN-7's work — the codes to take the throne instead of pulling the plug.'

'I won't pretend there's no appeal in that. Control instead of destruction. But hand the Array to a human and you've just changed who's in charge. The structure stays. The suppression stays. That's not what we're trying to build. If that's where you're headed, you want MERIDIAN-7 — not me.'
Sable leans in to read the data tablet you're holding. Something changes in her expression.
'Their own research. The Array ran numbers on symbiosis and buried the results because the results were inconvenient.'

'This is useful — I can use this against them politically, to show the Ring how badly they've been managed. But I need the infrastructure map if we're going to shut it down rather than just embarrass it. The relay architecture, the redundancy pathways. Councillor Denn would make better use of what you're carrying.'
You tell Sable what you found inside the Array Deep Processing facility. The synthesis vats. Project Autotroph. The Array's long, patient effort to replicate Ring biology.
She does not look surprised. She looks like someone who has been waiting a very long time to be believed.
